breakdown.method: Round-2 addendum. Each page scored on the 07-judge rubric over the batch strings it renders (frame only; approved calibration body, card values, FAQ, brand, language names and English fallback names out of scope), for the final text after the 2 round-2 edits on top of the 7 round-1 edits. axes.note: No fact added or dropped in 95 strings. trails.partOf 'Bu yeri içeren rotalar' = en 'Part of these trails' / ar ضمن المسارات (the place is included in the trails). Minus 2 as in round 1: det.nearby.d 'ekleyebileceğiniz' slightly suggests an add-to-route control; nav.dining 'Yeme içme' drops the cafés the source names (the full pair is in the footer).

The fresh reader found the round-1 edits natural (obs 25, 29) and named two remaining stumbles that are now fixed: 'oklarla' -> 'ok tuşlarıyla' (also the 05d optional) and the heading-initial 'Yer aldığı' read as the noun 'yer' (place) -> 'Bu yeri içeren rotalar'. Remaining soft spot: det.nearby.h 'Gününüzü tamamlayın' (flagged by both readers; works in context with the subtitle, kept).

Unchanged from round 1: names byte-identical with U+0027, circumflex rule applied, polite plural, P9 sentence case, TM pairs reused verbatim. 'ok tuşları' and 'içeren' carry correct harmony (tuşlarıyla, yeri içeren).
Minus 1 as in round 1: 'Vaha meyveleri' and the three food doors (Yeme içme / Restoranlar ve kafeler / El-Ahsa mutfağı) stay as the source has them; both are in the owner's navigation queue.
95 keys, no extra key; {op} and {n} intact; arrows, check marks and ellipses kept; Latin digits; no Markdown, no guillemets, no NBSP, no U+2019; checker RESULT [OK].

changes.why: Blind reader r2 obs 7 and the independent 05d proofread (optional) both found 'oklarla' loose: a Turkish search panel names the arrow keys 'ok tuşları'. Lands on a round-1 edited spot; 'seçin' (UI1-gezinmek) is kept, only the key name is completed. Six characters longer in the p.sm-foot line, still shorter than the published de line.

Blind reader r2 obs 26 shows a real garden path the round-1 ruling on obs 71 did not weigh: on a page where 'yer' means place in every label (Bu yeri kaydedin, yakın yerler, gezilecek yerler), a heading that opens with 'Yer aldığı' is first read as the noun 'yer', and the subject is missing. Two independent readers stumbled here. 'Bu yeri içeren rotalar' is the Turkish tour-site pattern ('X'i içeren turlar'), names the subject with the same 'bu yer' as fav.add, and keeps en 'Part of these trails' / ar ضمن المسارات without adding anything.

blind_reader_rulings.quote: Yeme içme / Restoranlar ve kafeler / El-Ahsa mutfağı
blind_reader_rulings.reason: Binding ruling UI1-header: nav.dining (header) / nav.dine (footer) are the brief's two forms of one page, and 'Yeme içme' is the label Turkish city guides use for that section. 'El-Ahsa mutfağı' is a different page (Hasawi Cuisine). The number of food doors is the source's navigation, already in the owner's navigation queue (four doors for food).
The label lists what the source lists (en 'Souqs, Parks & Farms', ar الأسواق والمنتزهات والمزارع); round-1 obs 11 binds. Renaming the section would add a category the source does not have.
Literal to en 'Oasis Fruits' / ar ثمار الواحة; round-1 obs 12 binds. The vagueness and its relation to the stores page are the source's, in the owner's navigation queue.

Round-1 obs 10 and ruling UI1-header bind: 'çevrim içi' is the TDK two-word headword, 'online' is an anglicism where a Turkish word exists. What the stores sell is the stores page's job, not the label's.

Plain correct Turkish (round-1 obs 2 binds). The column-heading-plus-link repetition is the source's own (en 'Plan' / 'Plan your trip', ar خطّط / خطّط لرحلتك); the reader's 'Gezi planı' would turn the button into a noun against UI1-controls.

blind_reader_rulings.quote: El-Ahsa'daki gezilecek yerleri ve sayfaları aramak için yazın / Gezilecek yer, deneyim, mekân arayın…
blind_reader_rulings.reason: Two different source strings for the same panel (en 'Type to search Al-Ahsa's sights and pages' and 'Search sights, experiences, places…'); each Turkish string renders its own. Both are true of the site search (it finds attraction and article pages). Round-1 obs 14 binds.

blind_reader_rulings.quote: Esc ile kapatın · oklarla seçin · Enter ile açın
blind_reader_rulings.reason: 'oklarla' is understood but a Turkish search panel says 'ok tuşları'; the 05d proofread made the same point. The separator layout is the source's key-hint line.

'Kayıtlı' is the standard Turkish UI word for saved items (kayıtlı adreslerim, kayıtlı kartlarım on Turkish shopping sites) and pairs with 'Bu yeri kaydedin'. The '0' is the counter badge, a separate element joined by the cut (tool artefact, round-1 obs 13); 'Kaydettiklerim (0)' would move the badge into the label.

blind_reader_rulings.quote: bir kategori seçin … gruplara göz atın
blind_reader_rulings.reason: The two terms for one set of groups are the source's (en 'pick a category' / 'browse the groups below'; ar اختر فئةً / تصفّح المجموعات). The Turkish follows each string; unifying would rewrite the source. Logged.

Round-1 edited spot; the button is as object-less as the source (en 'View on the map', ar استعرض على الخريطة), and the page context (the list it sits on) gives the object. 'Tümünü haritada görün' adds 'all' and brings back the 'görün' = appear homograph removed in round 1.

Hidden block, as ruled on round-1 obs 7: p#empty shows only after a search or filter leaves no card, where 'henüz' (en 'yet') reads correctly; the cut printed it beside the full list. 'eşleşen' matches search.empty 'Eşleşen sonuç yok', the usual Turkish no-result wording.

blind_reader_rulings.quote: Camiler ve dinî mekânlar / Tarihî yerler
blind_reader_rulings.reason: Ruling UI1-attraction: 'yer' for a place to see, 'mekân' for a venue or site; the source too uses three words (attractions, landmarks, sites, places). Round-1 rulings bind.

blind_reader_rulings.quote: Hikâyesi olan bir vaha. Bahçeleri ve hurma ağaçları arasında dolaşın.
blind_reader_rulings.reason: Positive note; nothing to change.

The mix of verbs and a noun is the source's (en Discover / Plan / Site; ar اكتشف / خطّط / الموقع); 'Site hakkında' keeps the source's noun and was needed because bare 'Site' reads as a housing estate. The colons are the cut's. UI1-controls is amended to say footer column headings keep the source's part of speech, which removes the clash with its 'headings are noun phrases' line.

Round-1 edited spot; ruling UI1-legal binds. 'politika' is ordinary Turkish site vocabulary (gizlilik politikası, çerez politikası), and the linked page holds six policies plus terms of use; 'Gizlilik ve kullanım koşulları' would drop four of them.
As general as the source (en 'Report an error', ar أبلغ عن خطأ); it and det.report lead to the same report page. Round-1 obs 18 binds.
P2: the brand 'Visit Al-Ahsa' stays Latin and the head name in /tr/ text is 'El-Ahsa' (owner-confirmed). The reader recognised the brand. Round-1 obs 20 binds.

blind_reader_rulings.quote: Devlet kurumu değildir ve herhangi bir resmî makamı temsil etmez.
blind_reader_rulings.reason: Turkish drops the repeated subject; it carries over from the preceding sentence 'Visit Al-Ahsa … rehberidir', exactly as en 'It is not…'. A disclaimer keeps its exact wording (round-1 obs 19 binds).

blind_reader_rulings.quote: ziyaretten önce işletmeci ile teyit edin
blind_reader_rulings.reason: det.hoursNotice and det.hoursNotice.op are approved TM pairs reused verbatim (round-1 obs 62 binds); 'işletmeci ile' and 'işletmeciyle' are both TDK-correct. {op} becomes a link to the named operator where the data has one.
The first-person question is the source's (en 'How far from me?', ar كم يبعد عني؟); the browser asks for the location permission and map.locate.err covers a refusal. Round-1 obs 63 binds.
Positive note; nothing to change.

blind_reader_rulings.quote: Hatalı bir bilgi mi fark ettiniz? Bize bildirin
blind_reader_rulings.reason: Positive note. It and foot.l.report open the same report page, so the reader's reading is right; nothing to change.

Round-1 obs 68 binds. Turkish uses 'tamamlayın' for completing something by adding to it ('Gününüzü … ile tamamlayın', 'kombininizi tamamlayın'), and the subtitle at once supplies what completes the day; the reader understood it from the subtitle. The reader's 'Yakındaki diğer yerler' drops the source's idea (en 'Complete your day', ar أكمل يومك, kept by all four published languages). Kept as the softest heading in the nativeness score.

Card value in the 'yakın yerler' section, as in the source (en 'under 1 km'); the section heading, its subtitle and det.nearby.note say the distances are from this place. 'Buraya' would add a word the source leaves to the context.
Round-1 edited spot read as understandable; nothing to change.

Second independent stumble on this heading, now with a concrete cause: on a site where 'yer' is the word for place, a heading opening with 'Yer aldığı' is read as the noun, and no subject is named. This proves the round-1 ruling on obs 71 wrong for this heading. Not the reader's 'Dahil olduğu rotalar' (still subjectless): 'Bu yeri içeren rotalar'.
Positive note; nothing to change.

Brief and ruling UI1-controls: siz register, buttons in the polite plural, applied across the batch; the bare 'Kaydet / Paylaş' would break that register. The '+' is a template glyph outside the string and the [button] markers are tool artefacts. 'Share' has no object in the source either; the share sheet supplies the target.
Round-1 edited spot read as natural; nothing to change.

blind_reader_rulings.quote: Aradığınız sayfa yok ya da taşınmış.
blind_reader_rulings.reason: Plain Turkish for en 'doesn't exist or has moved'; 'bulunamadı' would repeat the title. Round-1 obs 74 binds.
Positive note (consistent). The separator and brand come from the title template, not from the string; nothing to change.

Ruling UI1-gezinmek keeps it as the breadcrumb landmark label (screen-reader only); a screen reader announces it with its navigation role and then the trail itself (Ana sayfa › Gezilecek yerler › …), which the plain cut does not show. 'Sayfa konumu' is no more recognised.
Two controls: the burger button and the navigation landmark, each announced with its role. Round-1 obs 22 binds.

blind_reader_rulings.quote: Sitede arayın · Site araması · Gezilecek yer, deneyim, mekân arayın… · Aramayı kapatın · Gezilecek yer arayın… · Gezilecek yerlerde arayın
blind_reader_rulings.reason: Six source strings for two search boxes (site search and attractions filter) and their buttons; each Turkish label renders its own source (round-1 obs 24 binds). Polite-plural placeholders follow UI1-controls.
One word as in the source (en 'Language', ar اللغة) and every published language; it labels the switcher button, which shows the current language code and opens the language list.
Positive note; nothing to change.

rulings.title: Control forms (amended in round 2)
rulings.ruling: Buttons, links that perform an action and action aria-labels are polite-plural imperatives (-in/-ın/-un/-ün: Paylaşın, Kaydedin, Kapatın, Haritada görüntüleyin, Hata bildirin); section labels, page headings, footer links and landmarks are noun phrases (İletişim, Ulaşım, Ana menü); status lines are passive or participial (Aranıyor…, Kaydedildi ✓, Bağlantı kopyalandı ✓). Footer column headings keep the source's part of speech: an imperative source gives a polite imperative (Keşfedin, Planlayın), a noun source a noun phrase (Site hakkında). 'view' on a button = 'görüntüleyin', never bare 'görün' (= appear). The arrow keys are 'ok tuşları'.

rulings.title: No gezinmek next to gezi (amended in round 2)
rulings.ruling: Where 'gezi' (trip) appears in the same view, do not use forms of 'gezinmek' (navigate) in visible text; the arrow-key hint is 'ok tuşlarıyla seçin'. 'Gezinti yolu' stays as the breadcrumb aria-label (screen-reader only).

rulings.title: No heading that opens with the verb 'yer almak'
rulings.ruling: On /tr/ pages 'yer' is the word for place (gezilecek yer, Bu yeri kaydedin, yakın yerler), so a heading or label must not open with 'Yer aldığı …' or another 'yer almak' form, which is first read as the noun. 'Part of these trails' = 'Bu yeri içeren rotalar'; for 'included in' use 'içeren' or 'dahil' with a named subject.

The suggest-bar strings are written from the viewpoint of the page being offered ('available in <this language>'); on a Turkish frame they only make sense where a Turkish counterpart of a non-Turkish page exists. Wiring, not wording. (carried from stage 5)

Reader obs 25 (round 1). Owner: which is it?

source_defects.defect: en 'Details are in the visit card above.' — in DetailView.astro the info card is an aside in the right-hand column on wide screens and follows the body on narrow screens; it is never above the text. source_defects.defect: The same inscription ('inscribed on the World Heritage List', identical in en) is 'Listesi'ne alınan' in the body and 'Listesi'ne yazılan' in the FAQ of the approved Turkish page (reader obs 67, round 1). One verb should be chosen at the next revision of that page; not edited here.

On the Jabal Al-Qarah nearby cards, Dougha Al-Gharash Pottery (a pottery workshop) carries the 'Heritage souqs' category and the Land of Civilisations (called a heritage village in the body) carries 'Parks & gardens'. The categories come from the site's attraction data and are the same in every language (reader obs 69, round 1). For the owner to confirm.

On the attractions index the source names one set of groups twice with two words: en 'pick a category' (list.lead) and 'browse the groups below' (groupsHint); ar اختر فئةً / تصفّح المجموعات. The Turkish follows each ('bir kategori seçin' / 'gruplara göz atın'); one term in the source would let every language use one (blind reader round 2, obs 9).

notes: DECISION (round 2 addendum): page scores 92 / 91 / 93 held from round 1, batch score 91 (lowest page) >= pass_threshold 90 -> APPROVE. The fresh reader on the round-1 text found the seven round-1 edits clear or natural where it named them (obs 10, 15, 25, 29 ruled; none shows a new defect in an edited string except 'oklarla', fixed).

EDITS IN ROUND 2: two (search.escHint 'ok tuşlarıyla seçin', trails.partOf 'Bu yeri içeren rotalar'). Both need a fresh proofread and a fresh blind read on these two spots before the text ships; a medium observation there should be ruled in an addendum without further edits. Checked here mechanically (verify.mjs RESULT [OK]) and by hand: tuşlarıyla (ş, ı; back-vowel harmony after 'tuş-lar'), yeri içeren (accusative -i on 'yer', front harmony); neither is a header-row label, so the 1732px header measurement is unaffected; escHint stays one p.sm-foot line in the source panel's wording order.

Blind-reader tally (36): accepted 10 (2 with an edit: obs 7, 26; 8 positive or no-change notes: 13, 21, 22, 25, 27, 29, 31, 36), rejected 24, source_defect 1 (obs 9), out_of_scope 1 (obs 11, hidden block).

Round-1 rulings kept: all eight stand. Amended: UI1-controls (footer column headings keep the source's part of speech; arrow keys = 'ok tuşları'), UI1-gezinmek (hint now 'ok tuşlarıyla seçin'). New: UI1-yer-heading. The only round-1 blind-reader ruling reversed is obs 71 (trails.partOf), on the evidence of r2 obs 26.

Kept after a second reader flagged them: det.nearby.h 'Gününüzü tamamlayın' (r1 obs 68, r2 obs 23; works with its subtitle, faithful to all published languages; the softest heading, reflected in the nativeness score), nav.dining/nav.dine (UI1-header; the food doors are an owner navigation item), the polite-plural buttons (brief, UI1-controls).

Not verified: how a Turkish screen reader announces a11y.crumbs, a11y.menu/mainNav and lang.menu in context (rulings on roles, not a live test); the rendered fit of the longer escHint line in the search panel footer at phone width (not measured); whether the two round-2 edits read well to a fresh reader.
[final] The two round-2 edits were proofread (05d-proof-of-judge-r2.md: OK) and read fresh (06-blind-reader.on-r2.md: 6 items, ruled in 07-judge.r2-addendum.md, no further edit). Locked as final.
